verdict.rationale: LiveKit's docs show how to mint scoped, JWT-signed join tokens with per-permission grants (roomCreate, canPublish, subscribe-only) and expiry, and the CLI can access server APIs and create tokens. A community member also praised the 'get going' experience. The server-side room-creation step and the client SDK connect step are only implied, not shown as a documented end-to-end flow. missing for 10: an explicit server-side room/session creation API example, a documented client SDK connect call using the token, and evidence of a single short quickstart tying all three steps together.

support.subject: As a developer, I can create a session from my server, mint a scoped join token, and connect a client with the official SDK in a short documented flow

citations.quote: This token encodes the identity of a participant, name of the room, capabilities (for example, publishing audio, video, or data), and permissions (for example, permission to moderate a room). Access tokens are JWT-based and signed with your API secret to prevent forgery.
roomCreate — Permission to create or delete rooms
